statements.impact_statement: CVE-2024-6716 was assigned for LibTIFF issue #620, in which TIFFReadEncodedStrip() allocates a buffer whose size comes from a crafted file, so an application that reads untrusted TIFF files can run out of memory (https://gitlab.com/libtiff/libtiff/-/issues/620, https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2297636). LibTIFF resolved the issue with a documentation change only (https://gitlab.com/libtiff/libtiff/-/merge_requests/553): bounding memory use for untrusted input is the application's job, through the TIFFOpenOptionsSetMaxSingleMemAlloc() limit that LibTIFF provides since 4.5.0. Red Hat, the CNA that assigned the CVE, then rejected it as "Invalid security issue" (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2024-6716), and osv.dev lists it as withdrawn. No upstream code change exists for it. The current DHI libtiff6 package for Debian 13 (amd64 and arm64) is LibTIFF 4.7.0 and exports TIFFOpenOptionsSetMaxSingleMemAlloc.
